newsitem.title: USA: McVeigh plotted bomb to spark uprising - witness.
newsitem.headline: McVeigh plotted bomb to spark uprising - witness.

text.p: The star witness in the Oklahoma City bombing trial testified on Monday that accused bomber Timothy McVeigh told him he planned to blow up the Alfred P. Murrah federal building to touch off a "general uprising" against the U.S. government.

Michael Fortier said McVeigh, his former army buddy, also wanted to avenge the deaths of 80 Branch Davidian cult members in a fiery end to their confrontation with federal agents at Waco, Texas, in 1993.
The Oklahoma City federal building was destroyed by a huge truck bomb that killed 168 people on April 19, 1995 -- the second anniversary of the end of the Waco siege.

Fortier said McVeigh and alleged co-conspirator Terry Nichols singled out the Oklahoma City federal building for attack "because that was where the order for the attack on Waco had come." Nichols will be tried separately later.
McVeigh's other intention was to "cause a general uprising", to "knock some people off the fence" and push them into action against the government, Fortier testified.

He said that in their 1994 discussions, he asked McVeigh if he was concerned about what might happen to innocent people. McVeigh, refering to the "Star Wars" movies, said he considered all those people as "stormtroopers," Fortier said. The individuals may be innocent but "they were part of the Evil Empire and were guilty by association," he said.
